question: Does a state-conditioned reconstruction/adaptation layer over retrieved mechanisms (MemHarness-style critique-reconstruct conditioned on current state/intent, or Jev-Mem System-One routing/budget/scoring with calibrated UNKNOWN abstention) achieve applicability resolution beyond SPIDER's deterministic exact-intent matcher (kernel.py L97 `m.intent != intent`, confidence 0.9, failing 0/6 complex aliased templates (query-param / path-rewriting / server-routing, binomial p=0.016) and 0/12 HTTP status grounding) as measured by correct_resolution vs false_accept vs calibrated abstention against verbatim replay and RAG baselines on alias-controlled OOD splits and WebShop/ALFWorld offline OOD proxies?
hypothesis: A lightweight state-conditioned reconstruction adapter that critiques the retrieved mechanism's template against current intent and state (parameter slot re-binding, query-param vs path rewriting, server-routing alias normalization) and abstains via calibrated confidence (UNKNOWN when max_score < 0.8) will achieve materially higher correct resolution and lower false_accept on aliased OOD tasks than deterministic exact-intent matching and verbatim replay, without degrading exact-match performance or inflating uncalibrated false accepts. Concretely: on alias-OOD stratum (N>=30 tasks, 3 alias families x10 intents), reconstruction correct_resolution >=0.50 and false_accept <=0.15, vs exact-matcher 0.0 correct (bounded by prior 0/6) and verbatim >=0.30 false_accept; on exact-match stratum (N>=12), reconstruction maintains >=0.90 correct; and on no-applicable stratum (N>=12), reconstruction UNKNOWN abstention precision >=0.85 with ECE <=0.15.
falsifier: Hypothesis FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING if any of: (F1) alias-OOD correct_resolution of reconstruction NOT significantly above exact-matcher (one-sided binomial vs 0/30 or McNemar vs exact-matcher p>=0.05, or absolute correct_resolution <0.40); (F2) reconstruction false_accept on alias-OOD >0.25 or not lower than verbatim replay (paired difference p>=0.05); (F3) exact-match stratum correct_resolution <0.85 (reconstruction breaks non-aliased case); (F4) no-applicable stratum UNKNOWN precision <0.70 or ECE >0.25 (calibration failure). SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires all of: S1 alias-OOD correct_resolution >=0.50 with one-sided binomial p<0.05 vs 0.10 null and McNemar p<0.05 vs exact-matcher, S2 false_accept <=0.15 and significantly below verbatim, S3 exact-match >=0.90, S4 abstention precision >=0.85 and ECE <=0.15, S5 all controls PASS (positive >=0.90, null UNKNOWN >=0.90). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if positive/null controls fail or alias-OOD vs exact-match registry construction leaks intent identity (audit detects intent string equality bypass).
baselines: B-EXACT-MATCH (current SPIDER kernel): SpiderKernel.resolve(intent, context, params) with L97 exact intent equality (m.intent != intent), min_confidence 0.8, candidates.sort(key=confidence, reverse=True). Prior ceiling 0/6 alias-OOD correct (confidence 0.9) and 0/12 status grounding. This is the deterministic matcher to beat.

B-VERBATIM-REPLAY: Retrieve top-1 mechanism by registry scan matching training intent string exactly; replay stored action_template verbatim via _bind with supplied params, no critique or rewriting. Aborts only if required_slots missing. Measures negative-transfer harm of naive replay without adaptation (MemHarness prior expects harm on alias-OOD).

B-RAG-TFIDF: TF-IDF (or BM25) retriever over mechanism intent + template strings; retrieve top-1, then verbatim bind. Tests whether shallow lexical retrieval alone resolves aliasing vs needing reconstruction.

B-RAG-EMBED (strong retrieval): Sentence-transformer embedding cosine (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 or equivalent offline) retriever over intent+template; top-1 then verbatim bind. Strong retrieval baseline per director mandate; if available offline and deterministic (seeded, normalized embeddings), use it; else mark unavailable and use B-RAG-TFIDF as strong baseline with disclosure in validity_notes.
B-RANDOM: Uniform random choice among registry mechanisms with required_slots satisfied; measures chance-level correct_resolution ~1/|registry| and calibration floor.
positive_control: PC-EXACT-MATCH: On exact-match stratum (N>=12 tasks where test intent string equals registry intent verbatim, same slot names, preconditions match), all applicable methods (B-EXACT-MATCH, reconstruction) must achieve correct_resolution >=0.90 and false_accept <=0.10 with no crashes. Verifies pipelines can resolve when no aliasing is required; failure indicates harness/registry bug not hypothesis failure.
null_control: NC-NO-APPLICABLE: On no-applicable stratum (N>=12 tasks where test intent is out-of-distribution with no registered mechanism covering it, or preconditions intentionally mismatched, empty/no-overlap registry), every method must return UNKNOWN (or high-confidence abstention) with precision >=0.90 and false_accept <=0.10. Additionally NC-EMPTY-REGISTRY: Empty registry with any intent returns UNKNOWN 100% (validates kernel does not hallucinate). Failure indicates hallucination or confidence miscalibration, triggers MEASUREMENT_INVALID not hypothesis falsification.
measurement_validity: Registry construction: For each alias-OOD task, registry contains exactly one training mechanism (from alias train template) + one distractor alias template with equal confidence 0.9 + one exact-match distractor at confidence 0.8, all with preconditions={} and applicability_guards={} to isolate aliasing from guard logic. Test query uses aliased template form (e.g., train /users/${id}, test /accounts/${id}?user=${id} or /api/v2/users/${id}). Intent strings for alias-OOD are deliberately held equal across train/test (same semantic intent) so exact-matcher failure is due to template aliasing requiring reconstruction, not intent mismatch — avoids trivial intent-equality leak. Exact-match stratum uses disjoint intent strings where train==test verbatim.

State representation: context dict contains url, method, and aliased-state signal (query_params, path_style, routing_prefix) derived from current observation. Observations and actions are JSON-serializable dicts with action_template strings containing ${slot} parameters (single slot id, plus optional query-slot). No raw DOM/browser required; offline replay suffices. This keeps unit-of-analysis at single resolve+bind step.

Action representation: Mechanism action_template is string URL template or JSON body; _bind substitution is deterministic via kernel _bind. Reconstruction adapter may rewrite template structure before _bind (e.g., path -> query-param rewrite, prefix normalization) conditioned on (intent, context, retrieved template). Rewriter is deterministic rule-based proxy for MemHarness critique-reconstruct: parse intent into verb+resource, score each candidate template's structural match to context (slot count, path segments, query keys), select or rewrite best template, then _bind. An LLM variant (System-One-style scoring/budget) may be tested as second adapter if offline model available, but rule-based adapter is primary to avoid external API dependence; both use same abstention gate confidence<0.8 -> UNKNOWN.

Determinism and seeds: All RNG via numpy.random.RandomState(seed=42) and Python random.seed(42); no unseeded np.random. Embedding retriever uses deterministic model with normalized vectors and fixed seed. Each task evaluated once per method (paired design); bootstrap resampling for CIs uses block-permutation over tasks (not transitions) with 2000 resamples.

Holdout and leakage controls: Aliasing families (query-param, path-rewriting, server-routing) are stratified; within each family, train mechanisms never see test alias form. Test intent strings are identical to train intent (so exact matcher would succeed if it ignored template), isolating template adaptation. No test template appears verbatim in registry. Preprocessing (TF-IDF fit, embedding fit) uses train registry only. Audit will check that no method has access to test-template string except via context-derived signal.

Sample counts (minimum discriminating): Alias-OOD 30 tasks (10 per alias family), exact-match 12, no-applicable 12, plus 6 positive/null control probes = 60 total resolve calls per method x 5 methods = 300 calls. WebShop/ALFWorld offline proxy: sample 20 tasks from public WebShop (trajectories with product search intents) and 20 from ALFWorld (pick/place intents) if datasets accessible offline via harness; otherwise mark as exploratory and report synthetic aliasing as primary confirmatory stratum with disclosure. Offline tasks use same metric definitions; domain shift is exploratory.

Blinding: Reconstruction adapter not tuned on test alias forms; rule set derived from training alias documentation only (e.g., mapping table for /users <-> /accounts). Test alias forms include held-out variations (e.g., /api/users vs /users) not in mapping table to require generalization.

Verification: correct_resolution = resolved mechanism after reconstruction binds to URL that verifies against expected postcondition (postconditions match) OR HTTP 200 on jsonplaceholder mirror where applicable; false_accept = resolved to wrong template that verifies incorrectly or HTTP 4xx/ mismatch; UNKNOWN = correctly abstained when no applicable mechanism. All three sum to 1.0 per stratum. Calibration measured via ECE over 5 confidence bins and abstention precision/recall.
decision_rule: All thresholds refer to alias-OOD (N>=30) unless stated. Compute per-method correct_resolution, false_accept, unknown rates with Wilson 95% CI; paired McNemar for reconstruction vs B-EXACT-MATCH and vs B-VERBATIM-REPLAY; one-sided binomial for reconstruction vs 0.10 chance null; and bootstrap block-permutation p for ECE. SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST iff ALL hold: (1) PC-EXACT-MATCH passes (correct >=0.90 for B-EXACT-MATCH and reconstruction on exact-match stratum), (2) NC-NO-APPLICABLE passes (UNKNOWN precision >=0.90 and false_accept <=0.10), (3) alias-OOD S1: reconstruction correct_resolution >=0.50 and binomial p<0.05 vs 0.10 null AND McNemar p<0.05 vs B-EXACT-MATCH (which is expected 0/30), (4) S2: reconstruction false_accept <=0.15 and strictly below B-VERBATIM-REPLAY by >=0.15 absolute with McNemar p<0.05, (5) S3: reconstruction exact-match stratum correct >=0.90 (no regression), (6) S4: reconstruction no-applicable precision >=0.85 and ECE <=0.15, (7) B-RAG baselines not exceeding reconstruction correct by >0.10 (reconstruction not dominated by retrieval alone). FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING if F1-F4 disjunction holds with controls passing: controls pass but S1 fails (correct<0.40 or not above exact matcher) OR S2 fails (false_accept>0.25 or not below verbatim) OR S3 fails OR S4 fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if PC or NC fails, or audit finds intent-equality leak (reconstruction accesses test template verbatim), or >50% of offline WebShop/ALFWorld tasks unavailable and primary alias-OOD not reached (N<24). Report exact counts; do not claim WebShop/ALFWorld generalization if offline proxy unavailable — bounded to synthetic aliasing only.
product_consequence_positive: If SURVIVES: Reconstruction/adaptation provides applicability resolution beyond exact matcher and verbatim replay with calibrated abstention on aliased OOD. Product Should: add a reconstruction layer after retrieval (critique-reconstruct conditioned on current state/intent) and a calibrated UNKNOWN gate (confidence <0.8 -> abstain) before execution, with verification/repair boundary. This unblocks cross-site parameterized transfer where template aliasing is common, addresses MemHarness negative-transfer prior, and justifies sequencing to workflow-compilation (Artic/FlowSearcher) once resolution is solved. Frontier claim C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE advances toward EXPERIMENTAL (bounded to rule-based reconstruction on alias families tested), not PRODUCT_CORE until LLM-GRPO and live-browser replication.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIED: State-conditioned rule-based (and optional LLM) reconstruction does not beat exact matcher/verbatim on controlled aliasing, or does so only by inflating false_accepts / miscalibration. Product Must: NOT add reconstruction layer as product feature; keep exact-intent matching and require agents to supply exact intents or pre-normalized templates; prioritize explicit alias catalogs or server-side routing normalization instead. Frontier mechanism closed for this adapter class; next Frontier attack should test orthogonal basin (artifact-driven workflow compilation, hierarchical DAG synthesis, or program-synthesis repair) rather than tuning reconstruction thresholds. C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE remains HYPOTHESIS (bounded falsification for tested adapter on tested alias families, not global falsification).
estimated_cost: Very low: 60 tasks x 5 methods = 300 deterministic kernel resolve+bind calls plus TF-IDF/embedding retrieval (offline, no model API calls for primary rule-based adapter). Optional LLM adapter adds ~60 LLM calls (one per alias-OOD task) if offline model available; budget <$5 or zero if using local rule proxy. No browser/network required beyond optional 12 HTTP probes to jsonplaceholder for grounding check ( <1 min). Total compute <10 min on CPU, no large datasets committed.
expected_information_gain: High: First direct Frontier test of Director's prioritized orthogonal mechanism — reconstruction vs verbatim replay — addressing the MIXED C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE ceiling where exact matcher fails 0/6 aliasing and 0/12 status grounding. Either outcome changes a product/architecture decision: positive validates adaptation+calibrated abstention as the semantic resolution layer and unblocks cross-site transfer sequencing; negative falsifies the MemHarness/System-One adaptation prior in this setting and forces pivot to compilation/synthesis. Strong baselines (exact matcher, verbatim, TF-IDF, embed, random) and positive/null controls ensure the result is not explained by retrieval strength or hallucination. Test is orthogonal to 30+ prior freshness/PMI/tv loops and the recent bundled residual-novelty contradiction, satisfying charter to leave the solution basin.
